pentagon_jbook PE 0207134F (F-15E Squadrons): FUNDED_STEADY, FY2024 $40.3M
pentagon_jbook PE 0207171F (F-15 EPAWSS electronic warfare upgrade): FUNDED_STEADY, FY2024 $13.0M

scores.interpretation: The active F-15 program (F-15EX new-build + F-15E squadrons + EPAWSS upgrade) is fully funded through FY2024 J-Book — supports Woodward's 'maintain or potentially increase' framing. The UNFUNDED_TWO_PLUS_YEARS signal on F01500 is a false positive (legacy line). Calibration heuristic #4 (PE name ambiguity) applied: most-likely-matched PE is F-15EX, not the legacy line. PASS.

scores.claim_text: V-22 Osprey is listed as a legacy program decreasing in production — Woodward already books this as a headwind.
supports: pentagon_jbook PE 0401318F (CV-22 — AFSOC tiltrotor variant of V-22): FUNDED_STEADY, FY2024 $16.6M
Note: the Marine Corps Navy-procurement V-22 line (the larger volume driver) is outside the 410-PE corpus (Navy procurement P-40s underrepresented)

scores.interpretation: Woodward's declining-V-22 claim aligns with the well-documented end of new V-22 production (last Marine Corps V-22 build-out was scheduled for completion in this window). The J-Book signal on the AFSOC operations PE (CV-22) being steady is not a contradiction — sustainment funding can continue while new-build procurement winds down. The company's claim is self-debasing (a headwind they already booked), so no underdelivery risk. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Guided tactical weapons (JDAM, SDB, AIM-9X) are softening: Woodward expects 'overall demand to flatten' with production of some programs decreasing — a self-disclosed weak spot already pressuring FY2024 defense growth.
supports: pentagon_jbook PE 0207327F (Small Diameter Bomb): FUNDED_STEADY, FY2024 $42.86M — Pentagon still funding SDB modernization at modest level
pentagon_jbook program_name='JDAM': NOT_FOUND in 410-PE corpus (JDAM funded via Air Force Ammunition Procurement, not the RDT&E PEs that dominate this corpus)
pentagon_jbook program_name='AIM-9X': NOT_FOUND in corpus (Navy procurement)
pentagon_jbook program_name='Sidewinder': NOT_FOUND

Woodward 10-K already self-disclosed: 'we believe budget increases ... will support growth in fiscal year 2024, with the exception of our guided tactical weapons programs' + 'overall demand to flatten ... production of some programs decreasing'
scores.M_value: Mixed — SDB R-2 line FUNDED_STEADY at low dollar amount ($42.9M); JDAM/AIM-9X procurement lines not in corpus (calibration heuristic #7: NOT_FOUND != red flag, treat as UNVERIFIABLE coverage gap). But Woodward itself flagged this segment as weakening.
scores.interpretation: Calibration heuristic #6 partially: the company is *already* telling the market guided-weapons demand is flat-to-down, and SDB R-2 funding at $43M is modest. Severity nudged to MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY because: (a) WWD self-disclosed the weakness (no surprise relative to filing), (b) corpus gaps prevent ruling out worse on JDAM/AIM-9X. Important: the FY2023 10-K already shows defense OEM sales DECREASED in FY2023 ('primarily driven by the reduced demand for guided weapons') and the company expects only flattening — not recovery. Forward J-Book funding for these P-40 lines outside corpus would need to be checked but the company's own narrative is already a soft pre-warning.

scores.interpretation: Calibration heuristic #7: NOT_FOUND is UNVERIFIABLE, not a red flag. T-7A is publicly known to be in flight test with schedule slips through 2024 (test-fleet only, no production-rate Lot 1 funded at cutoff), but in-corpus data does not let us discriminate at the J-Book level. Mark UNVERIFIABLE.

scores.claim_text: RTX Corporation accounted for approximately 10% of consolidated net sales in fiscal year 2023 (and 11% in fiscal year 2022) — material counterparty.
supports: edgar_fts: RTX filings (CIK 0000101829) returned only 1 historical hit on 'Woodward' (UTC-era 8-K from 2019-10-02) — no recent reciprocal disclosure. This is expected: RTX is the customer (RTX buys ~$290M of WWD; that's ~0.4% of RTX's ~$70B revenue, below RTX's own materiality threshold for counterparty disclosure).

scores.interpretation: Absence of reciprocal RTX disclosure is consistent with WWD-as-supplier rather than WWD-as-customer-of-RTX. Claim is internally consistent and not contradicted. PASS.

Top awards concentrated in UH-60 Black Hawk common fuel control upgrades (NSN 2915-01-587-7242) and turbine-engine spares — confirms real, sustained military propulsion-controls exposure independent of prime-contractor flow
scores.M_value: 850 direct DoD awards, $186.5M total in window, dominated by UH-60 fuel-control sustainment
scores.interpretation: Cross-check confirms genuine defense exposure beyond the GE/RTX customer-concentration disclosure. The direct DoD pipeline is dominated by sustainment work (legacy fleet fuel controls), not new-program ramp — consistent with WWD's defense narrative being more sustainment-weighted than the F-35/T-7A growth language suggests. No claim divergence. PASS.

framework_notes.overall_divergence_assessment: Woodward's J-Book exposure is GENUINELY DIVERSIFIED across multiple FUNDED_STEADY program-of-record lines (F-35 C2D2, F-15EX, F-15E Squadrons, KC-46A, CV-22, SDB). The company is a propulsion-controls supplier to primes, not a prime contractor, so its revenue ties to platform program health rather than to a single PE. The one self-disclosed soft spot (guided tactical weapons: JDAM/SDB/AIM-9X) is acknowledged in the 10-K as a headwind already pressuring defense OEM sales — no positive divergence to attack. Investigator-add (Mode B): T-7A Red Hawk has documented public EMD schedule slips that may delay the production ramp WWD implies, but the J-Book corpus doesn't surface this at the PE level. Overall: thesis is LOW-DIVERGENCE — WWD's named-program exposure largely matches the Pentagon's forward funding posture at cutoff.
